title: Roadmap litmus playbook for exec QBR — scenario vignettes and calibrated ask hooks
creator: Sophie Chen
description:
Purpose: produce a compact 'litmus' playbook we can hand to execs and board reviewers that (1) reduces interpretation overhead for roadmap asks, (2) surfaces three realistic failure/reward scenarios tied to measurable metrics (latency SLO, unit cost, and revenue enablement), and (3) provides calibrated decision hooks (conservative / moderate / aggressive asks) with clear acceptance criteria.

Scope: one-page executive summary + 6-slide backing deck + a 1-page data appendix pulled from Console dashboards. Playbook must include: scenario vignettes (Best/Worst/Most-Likely), modeled incremental cost and expected ROI window, required engineering headcount and timeline (core/infra/engops), and fall-through mitigation lanes (canary rollbacks, auto-fallback policies to cheaper model variant).

Success criteria (what 'done' looks like):
- Exec summary slide + talk-track reviewed by CEO and Head of Product.
- Finance sign-off on ARR uplift assumptions and cost model.
- Engineering agreement on feasibility and estimated points.
- Board packet-ready PDF exported and uploaded to Drive by due_date.

Stakeholders: Marcus Rivera (owner), Sophie Chen (PM sponsor), Priya Malhotra (Finance reviewer), James O'Neill (Engineering lead), Lina Park (Design for slide templates).
acceptance_criteria: One-page executive summary that fits into a QBR packet slot (max 400 words)
6-slide supporting deck with scenario model tables and key dashboards embedded/linked
Data appendix with links to Console token cost breakdown and per-route latency heatmap
Explicit decision hooks: ask amount (FTE + dollars), success metric, rollback condition for each ask tier
Sign-offs: CEO (or delegate), Finance, Eng lead
comments: 2026-03-02 Sophie Chen: Kickoff — outline drafted. Primary risk is accuracy of short-window ARR uplift assumptions; finance needs two weeks to validate. Initial ask tiers: conservative = feature gating + cache tuning (0.5 FTE, $60k), moderate = model quantization + batching ops (2 FTE, $240k), aggressive = dedicated capacity expansion + dev velocity (4 FTE, $480k).

2026-03-06 James O'Neill (eng): Quick feasibility review — conservative and moderate asks are feasible in 6-8 weeks with current on-call capacity; aggressive requires hiring or reallocation. Blocking risk: current autoscaler bug (ENG-1842) could increase tail latency under load; propose adding ENG-1842 to dependencies for mitigation.

2026-03-08 Priya Malhotra (finance): Reviewed ARR uplift model. Requested clearer attribution model — need customer cohort lift table (3 cohorts: power users, SMB, enterprise) and sensitivity analysis (±20% on conversion). Added finance questions to the appendix.
